result.title: Notice to Prospective Respondents February 3, 2022
result.summary: Texas Municipal Retirement System (TMRS) invites proposals for non-discretionary general investment consulting services under its February 3, 2022 RFP. Proposals were due by 5:00 p.m. CST on March 3, 2022; late submissions would not be considered, and respondents were directed to the transmittal instructions. Written clarification questions were due February 27, 2022, to ConsultantSearch2022@tmrs.com, with responses shared with confirmed respondents. Verbal statements by TMRS personnel are not binding, and unauthorized contact with TMRS Board members or staff may result in disqualification. The contents list sections covering the event schedule, introduction, TMRS program, general information and minimum requirements, scope of services, transmittal instructions, questions and requested attachments, fee proposal, and appendix, including a draft investment consulting services agreement and exhibits.

result.title: SECTION II
result.summary:
SECTION II
INTRODUCTION
TMRS is issuing an RFP for non-discretionary General consulting services — see Section V “Scope of Services” for more detail on the consulting mandate. Section VI “Transmittal Instructions” provides information on how to respond to this RFP. Section VII “RFP Questions & Requested Attachments” and Section VIII “Fee Proposal” are sections of the RFP which respondents are requested to review and provide responses to.
5

result.title: SECTION III
result.summary: TMRS is a $36 billion statewide hybrid cash balance retirement system established in 1947, providing retirement, disability, and death benefits to employees of approximately 900 Texas cities. It is governed by a six-member Board of Trustees appointed by the Texas Governor to six-year terms. TMRS is 89.5% funded and has a 6.75% target portfolio return. Target allocations are 35% global public equity, 20% non-core fixed income, 12% real estate, 12% other public and private markets, 10% private equity, 6% core fixed income, and 5% hedge funds. Further information is available at tmrs.com, and the Investment Policy Statement is linked at the provided TMRS URL.

result.title: SECTION IV
key_items: A. Issuing Office; B. Purpose of Document; C. Commitment of TMRS; D. Period of Contract
F. Principal Firm Responsibility; G. Cost of Preparing Proposal
result.summary: TMRS issues this RFP for non-discretionary general investment consulting from firms serving large public pension plans. TMRS may amend or cancel it; submissions create no rights or obligation to award a contract. Any resulting agreement is governed by Texas law, and the negotiated initial term begins after Board approval. TMRS may verify proposal information. Proposals must name responsible principals; respondents bear proposal and presentation costs. The proposal period starts February 3, 2022, and ends upon cancellation or contract execution. Firms may not contact trustees or staff except as authorized; existing providers should limit contact to ordinary business interactions. Eligibility requires current advice to at least five public pension plans over $5 billion and two over $20 billion; written fiduciary commitment; acceptance of contractual negligence and Prudent Expert standards; Texas law and venue; SEC investment-adviser registration with Forms ADV Parts 1 and 2; required licenses and certifications; no material conflicts with TMRS or State Street; fiduciary and liability insurance; willingness to sign an agreement substantially like Exhibit A; and adequate operational controls.

result.title: SECTION V
key_items: SCOPE OF SERVICES FOR GENERAL CONSULTING
1. Fiduciary Standard of Care General Investment Advisory Services.
result.summary: The consultant, hired by and reporting to the Board, must provide competent, objective, independent investment advice while working with staff and supporting Trustee education, consistent with TMRS objectives and applicable laws. Services include annual asset-allocation review and recommendations (formal studies historically every three years; completed 2019, next planned 2022), and periodic asset-liability reviews (roughly every 3–6 years; next planned 2022, separately priced). The consultant reviews proposed initiatives for policy consistency; recommends performance goals, objectives and benchmarks; analyzes and reports returns, including attribution; and helps prepare Board/committee agendas and attend meetings (about five meetings and one retreat in 2022). It also provides research-based education, reporting guidance, presentations and requested research, analysis, advice and recommendations; assists with custodian-bank and securities-lending evaluations; and identifies implementation-related operational, accounting, administrative and legal issues or resources. For public-market managers, it supports research, screening, selection criteria, analysis, interviews, comparisons, implementation, monitoring, oversight questions, fee/guideline advice, termination recommendations and due-diligence trips.

result.title: SECTION VI
key_items: A. Introduction; B. Written Response and Proprietary Information
B. Written Response and Proprietary Information
result.summary: TMRS requests concise responses and may seek additional information; it need not award a contract, proposals will not be returned, and respondents must first document compliance with Section IV-I minimum requirements. Proposals must answer all questions in order. Disclosure and confidentiality are governed by applicable law, including the Texas Public Information Act; TMRS may use proposal ideas regardless of selection. Submit three electronic copies—complete, confidential/proprietary, and public—by 5:00 p.m. CST on the cover-letter date to ConsultantSearch2022@tmrs.com. If email is impractical, contact Kristin Qualls to arrange FTP delivery. Respondents must confirm receipt. The transmittal letter must be on official letterhead and include: certification that no associated Texas/TMRS personnel helped prepare the proposal except as allowed; agreement to RFP terms; a six-month validity guarantee or until contract approval; exceptions and required agreement revisions; contact details; and confirmation that the signer can bind the firm. The letter and proposal must be signed by an authorized person able to answer questions and clarify the proposal.

result.title: SECTION VII
key_items: Please provide the following requested attachments:
result.summary: The RFP requests sample prior proposals; a firm-services presentation covering history, ownership, organization, clients, performance and proposed staff; public-plan clients/assets; comparable client references; ethics, trading, ESG and diversity policies; terminated/nonrenewed clients; investment and operational due-diligence reports; manager recommendations, assets and database size; capital-market, peer and performance reports; five-year return, risk, inflation, correlation and portfolio assumptions; ownership details and conflicts; and assigned-team resumes. Questions cover organizational changes, ownership, business lines, revenue, research investment, discretionary services, money management, broker-dealer activity, soft dollars, conflicts and firewalls; legal/regulatory history, examinations, fees, conduct, personal trading and insurance. They ask about client base and services, custody/securities lending, subcontractors, service evaluation and trustee education; staffing, retention, communications, workloads, backup, team roles, presentations and other clients; research structure and sources; diligence, approvals, coverage, fee discounts, manager ethics, monitoring and capacity allocation; accounting, performance, fee tracking, onboarding and service levels; and further trustee education and recommended additional considerations.

result.title: Please provide the following questions regarding consulting services:
result.summary: The questionnaire covers the firm’s investment-policy, asset-allocation, risk-management, and portfolio-review processes, requesting allocation examples and return/volatility forecasts for TMRS’s target portfolio. It asks about actuarial-consultant relationships, liability and asset-liability studies, alpha budgets, and strategies across public equities, fixed income, private credit, cash, and private markets—including leverage, liquidity, illiquidity limits, and investments such as private equity, real estate, infrastructure, mining, and energy transition. It also addresses hedge funds, gold, digital assets, ESG, capital-market assumptions, inflation, correlations, and forecast horizons, plus risk factors, tail-risk mitigation, overlays, and tactical planning. Performance-measurement questions cover data collection and checks, reporting timelines, customized reports, attribution and portfolio aggregation, peer comparisons, and access to comparison data. Manager-search questions address selection criteria and methods, databases and data verification, client updates, ongoing monitoring, retained-manager information access, and termination recommendations.

nodes.title: Please provide the following questions regarding consulting services: (intro)
nodes.summary: The questionnaire asks about the firm’s investment-policy and asset-allocation processes, including investment philosophy/objectives, benchmarks, risk policies, portfolio analysis and ongoing review. It requests allocation examples and return/volatility forecasts for TMRS’s target portfolio, plus actuarial-consultant relationships, liability studies, ALM frequency and responses to expected-return shortfalls. Topics include alpha budgeting; active versus passive public equities, performance and completion strategies; fixed income, private credit, leverage, liquidity and inflation protection; cash policy; and private-market allocations, illiquidity thresholds, relative weights and strategies spanning private equity, real estate, infrastructure, mining, energy transition and other alternatives. It also covers hedge funds, gold, cryptocurrencies and digital assets; ESG advice and integration; capital-market assumption updates, inflation, mean reversion, correlations and forecast horizons. Finally, it asks about portfolio risk frameworks, factors and sectors, tail-risk mitigation, overlays and tactical planning, with supporting client examples and experience.

nodes.title: 2. Specific Information Regarding Performance Measurement
nodes.summary: TMRS’s general investment consultant currently generates and reports investment performance. The section specifies a 24-day reporting turnaround after receipt of custodial data and asks about data-collection procedures, online communication with custodians, and quality and reasonableness checks. It also covers available performance reports and attribution at security, asset-type, and portfolio levels; the ability to aggregate or disaggregate the full portfolio for any requested period, including before the consulting relationship; and quarter-end reporting timelines. Peer evaluation questions address the availability of comparable funds based on size, liability structure, investment objective, and actuarial discount rate, analysis at total-fund and asset-class levels, use of the Wilshire Trust Fund Universe Comparison Service, and TMRS staff access to its data. The section also asks whether client reports can be customized.

nodes.title: 3. Specific Information Regarding Manager/Advisor Search
nodes.summary: The text requests details about the firm’s public-market investment manager/advisor search and oversight processes: how managers are evaluated and selected across personnel and organization, investment philosophy, styles and products, research capabilities, financial condition, assets under management, client service, and responsibility; the methodology and data sources used to assess value-adding ability; manager-search databases, including update frequency, information sources, client notification of changes, external-data verification, and staff visit frequency; ongoing monitoring of administrative matters such as staff turnover, mergers, and financial soundness, how clients are notified, and whether they can access updates on retained managers; and the process and criteria for recommending termination.

result.title: SECTION VIII FEE PROPOSAL
result.summary: Section VIII requests a total all-inclusive annual fee for all Scope of Services and other potential contract costs, for a multi-year term to be negotiated. Respondents should detail any per-report charges for additional TMRS services, including Asset/Liability studies and the Practice & Performance report required by Texas Statute §802.109. Section IX includes a draft Investment Consulting Services Agreement between TMRS and a consultant, effective on a date to be agreed in 2022. Its recitals describe TMRS’s purpose and status, the Board’s fiduciary responsibility to invest assets for members and beneficiaries, and the consultant’s qualifications and resources. Article 1 incorporates the recitals, engages the consultant to provide services under the agreement, and establishes the consultant as an independent contractor—not a TMRS employee, partner, or joint venturer—who cannot bind TMRS and is responsible for its own taxes and withholdings.

result.title: Recitals
result.summary: The appendix contains a draft Investment Consulting Services Agreement, effective on a date to be filled in during 2022, between an unnamed consultant and the Texas Municipal Retirement System (TMRS). The recitals describe TMRS as a Texas governmental pension entity providing retirement, death, and survivor benefits to municipal employees and beneficiaries; the Board’s duty to hold assets in trust for members, annuitants, and beneficiaries and invest consistently with TMRS’s mission; and the consultant’s experience, expertise, and resources to advise TMRS staff and the Board on institutional portfolio management. The parties agree to the agreement’s terms in consideration of mutual promises and fees.

result.title: Agreement
result.summary: The agreement engages the Consultant as an independent contractor to provide investment consulting services, with no authority to bind TMRS and responsibility for its own taxes and obligations. It establishes fiduciary duties, standards of loyalty and prudence, restrictions on conflicts and benefits, services in Exhibit A, assigned personnel, and indemnification obligations. It governs confidentiality, legally required disclosures, public-records and open-meetings requirements, use and retention of work materials, third-party intellectual property, and record return or destruction. Fees are paid quarterly in arrears without expense reimbursement; the agreement has a stated term, and TMRS may terminate at any time with prorated payment and transition cooperation. It covers Consultant representations, disclosures and reporting, insurance, and open-meeting participation, plus amendments, assignment, beneficiaries, Texas law and venue, severability, notices, claims procedures, and other standard terms. Exhibits address services, personnel, and Consultant disclosures.

nodes.title: ENGAGEMENT
key_items: DRAFT Agreement for Investment Consulting Services
nodes.summary: Article 1 incorporates the recitals into the agreement and retains the Consultant to provide investment consulting services under its terms. The Consultant and its personnel are independent contractors, not TMRS employees, partners, or joint venturers. The Consultant may not claim to be a TMRS employee or bind TMRS to agreements, and is responsible for its taxes, withholdings, and other business-related statutory or contractual obligations, including workers’ compensation insurance. Article 2 begins, but no provisions are provided.

nodes.title: FIDUCIARY STANDARDS AND SCOPE OF SERVICES; INDEMNIFICATION
nodes.summary: The consultant is a fiduciary to TMRS, its Board, participants, beneficiaries, and trust assets, must act loyally and prudently under applicable law and Board policies, and is barred from self-dealing, adverse representation, compromised judgment, or receiving transaction-related benefits. Services are specified in Exhibit A. The consultant indemnifies and defends TMRS and related persons for specified misconduct and intellectual-property or trade-secret violations; these duties survive contract changes or termination. The agreement identifies assigned personnel and TMRS’s representative, with consultation required before personnel changes. Confidential information may be used only to provide services and disclosed only with consent or as legally required, subject to notice and cooperation; public-records and open-meetings laws may apply. TMRS may use and retain consultant work, while the consultant must address third-party copyrights and follow document-return, retention, and destruction-notice rules. These confidentiality-related duties survive expiration or termination. Fees are annual, invoiced quarterly in arrears, with no expense reimbursement. The agreement has a stated term and TMRS may terminate at any time on written notice, paying a prorated fee for the partial quarter.

nodes.title: FEES
nodes.summary: The section covers Consultant’s participation in open TMRS meetings; TMRS’s and its advisers’ rights to use, retain, and disclose work materials, with source identification and copyright notices for third-party content; return and retention of records, advance notice before destruction, and surviving obligations. It sets a blank annual fee and invoice recipient, quarterly payment in arrears, no expense or travel reimbursement, and a blank term end date. TMRS may terminate by written notice at any time, with a prorated fee for a partial quarter and good-faith transition cooperation. Consultant gives representations and warranties regarding independence, disclosures and history, qualifications and registration, regulatory notices, legal and ethical compliance, resources, authorization, status, and prohibited benefits, and must report changes. Other provisions address insurance and tail coverage, amendments, assignment, beneficiaries, Texas law and venue, severability, exhibits, entire agreement, counterparts, notices, claims procedures without waiving sovereign immunity, signature blocks, and Exhibits A–C for services, personnel, and disclosures.

nodes.title: ARTICLE 4
nodes.summary: Consultant may participate in meetings of the TMRS Board or committees open under Texas open-meetings law. TMRS and its auditors and other advisers may use and retain Consultant’s written work and reports and may disclose them to third parties; Consultant must identify sources and provide copyright notices for third-party copyrighted material. Consultant acknowledges TMRS is a Texas state entity subject to the Act. On request, Consultant must return TMRS-provided records, subject to regulatory indefinite-retention requirements. Consultant must retain work papers and reports for at least five years or any longer period required by TMRS policy, Texas law, or court order, and notify TMRS before destruction and ask whether it wants the materials. Specified obligations survive expiration or termination. The annual fee and invoice recipient are blank; fees are paid quarterly in arrears, with no expense or travel reimbursement, and invoices are sent at each quarter’s end. The term’s end date is blank. TMRS may terminate immediately by written notice at any time, with or without cause; Consultant receives a prorated fee for the partial quarter.

nodes.title: TERM
nodes.summary: The section addresses consultant access to public TMRS meetings; TMRS’s use, retention, and disclosure of work materials; third-party content notices; return and retention of records, destruction notice, and surviving obligations. It provides for quarterly fees in arrears, no expense or travel reimbursement, blank fee and invoice details, and a term ending on a blank date unless terminated earlier. TMRS may terminate at any time by written notice, with prorated fees for a partial quarter and good-faith transition cooperation. Consultant representations and warranties cover independence, disclosures and relevant history, registration and qualifications, regulatory notices, legal and ethical compliance, resources, authorization, status, and prohibited benefits, with prompt reporting of changes. Miscellaneous terms cover insurance and tail coverage, amendments, assignment, beneficiaries, Texas law and venue, severability, exhibits, entire agreement, counterparts, notices, and claims procedures without waiving sovereign immunity. The section also includes signature blocks and identifies Exhibits A–C for services, personnel, and disclosures.

nodes.title: Consultant Records, Fees, and Agreement Term
nodes.summary: Consultant may participate in TMRS Board or committee meetings open to the public. TMRS and its representatives may use and retain work materials and may disclose them to third parties; Consultant must provide sources and copyright notices for third-party content and acknowledges TMRS is subject to the Act. At TMRS’s request, Consultant must return TMRS-provided records, subject to applicable retention requirements. Consultant must retain work papers and reports for at least five years or any longer required period, notify TMRS before destruction, and ask whether TMRS wants the materials. Specified obligations survive expiration or termination. The annual fee and invoice recipient are blank; fees are paid quarterly in arrears, with no reimbursement for expenses or travel, and invoices are sent at each quarter’s end. The Agreement starts on the date specified above and expires on a blank date in 202__, unless earlier terminated under Article 4.

nodes.title: 4.2 Termination.
nodes.summary:
4.2 Termination. TMRS may terminate this Agreement immediately upon written notice to Consultant for any reason or for no reason at any time during the Term of this Agreement; provided, however, that Consultant shall be entitled to receive a fee for the partial quarter determined by applying the ratio of days elapsed in the calendar quarter to the total number of days in the quarter multiplied by the regularly computed full quarterly fee. Upon termination of
30this Agreement for any reason, Consultant agrees to cooperate in good faith with respect to any transition by TMRS to another consultant.

nodes.title: ARTICLE 5
nodes.summary: ARTICLE 5

nodes.title: REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES
key_items: 5.1 Representations, Warranties and Covenants by Consultant.
nodes.summary: Consultant (including Assigned Personnel for specified provisions) makes warranties and covenants that survive execution and termination. It has no undisclosed relationships that could impair independent judgment or create impropriety; except as disclosed in Exhibit C, it and relevant principals have no adverse investment-related ethics, litigation, investigation, licensing, penalty, or criminal history. Consultant will remain a registered investment adviser, and its representative and key personnel are qualified. Where legally permitted, it will notify TMRS in writing within five business days of specified extraordinary governmental, regulatory, or exchange proceedings affecting its performance or relevant investment professionals. It does not and will not boycott Israel or energy companies, has knowingly complied with the Texas Public Information Act, and has adequate resources. The Agreement does not conflict with its obligations, is duly authorized and binding, and Consultant is properly organized and in good standing, with Texas authority if foreign. It will immediately report changes to any Article 5 representation or warranty and has not offered, nor intends to offer, prohibited benefits to TMRS trustees or employees, except as legally permitted.

nodes.title: ARTICLE 6
nodes.summary: ARTICLE 6

nodes.title: MISCELLANEOUS
nodes.summary: Consultant must maintain combined errors-and-omissions and fiduciary-liability insurance at least at the specified (blank) million-dollar amount, provide certificates or other satisfactory evidence on request, and fund at least one year of tail coverage for claims-made policies after termination. The agreement covers written amendments and waivers, Texas-law compliance, no assignment or delegation, permitted successors and assigns, limited beneficiaries, non-substantive headings, Texas law and Travis County venue, severability, incorporated exhibits, entire-agreement terms, counterparts, and no waiver through inaction. Where applicable and not preempted, Texas Government Code Chapter 2260 governs unresolved contract claims; TMRS’s Executive Director or designee reviews and negotiates claims, without waiving sovereign immunity or TMRS’s right to seek court relief. These provisions survive as stated. Notices must be written and sent by specified mail, courier, or fax methods; TMRS’s Austin address and the blank Consultant address are provided. The agreement includes signature blocks for Consultant and TMRS Executive Director David B. Wescoe, and lists Exhibits A (Scope of Services), B (Consultant’s Representative and Key Personnel), and C (Consultant’s Disclosures).

nodes.title: 6.1 Insurance.
key_items: 6.1.1 Errors and Omissions and Fiduciary Liability Insurance.
nodes.summary: Consultant must maintain combined errors-and-omissions and fiduciary-liability insurance of at least the stated (blank) million-dollar amount, provide satisfactory evidence on request, and, for claims-made coverage, fund at least one year of extended reporting or tail coverage after the Agreement ends. Insurance certificates must be delivered immediately upon request. Amendments and waivers generally require a signed writing; Consultant must cooperate with amendments required by Texas law. Consultant may not assign or delegate the Agreement or its duties, rights, or obligations; it binds the parties and their permitted successors and assigns. The Agreement benefits only TMRS and Consultant; headings are non-substantive. Texas law governs, venue is in competent state courts in Travis County, and this provision survives. Invalid provisions do not affect the remainder. Exhibits are incorporated by reference. The Agreement is the entire agreement, supersedes prior agreements, and may be amended only in a writing signed by all parties. Counterparts are permitted, and inaction does not waive rights or approve breaches. Disputes are subject, where applicable and not preempted, to Texas Government Code Chapter 2260.

nodes.title: Contract Terms and Legal Provisions
nodes.summary: Consultant must provide TMRS with insurance certificates upon request. Amendments and waivers generally require a signed writing, and Consultant must cooperate with amendments needed to comply with Texas law. Consultant cannot assign or delegate the agreement; it binds the parties and permitted successors and assigns and benefits only TMRS and Consultant. Headings are for reference only. Texas law governs, with venue in Travis County courts, and this provision survives termination or other changes. Invalid provisions do not affect the remainder of the agreement. Exhibits are incorporated by reference. The agreement is the complete understanding on Consultant’s services and payment, supersedes prior agreements, and may be executed in counterparts. A party’s inaction does not waive rights or approve a breach.

nodes.title: 6.12 Dispute Resolution.
nodes.summary: If Texas Government Code Chapter 2260 applies and is not preempted, its dispute-resolution process will be used for Consultant’s breach-of-contract claims that cannot be resolved in ordinary business. TMRS’s Executive Director or designee will review the claim and any counterclaim and negotiate toward resolution. The Agreement and TMRS representatives’ related conduct do not waive TMRS’s sovereign immunity, and TMRS retains the right to seek redress in court. This section survives termination, expiration, renewal, extension, or amendment of the Agreement.

nodes.title: 6.13 Notices.
nodes.summary: Notices under the Agreement must be written and properly addressed, and may be sent by prepaid first-class U.S. mail, nationally recognized courier for hand delivery, or fax. They take effect upon delivery, or for fax, receipt during the addressee’s business hours of a complete, legible transmission. Parties may change their addresses by notice under these rules. TMRS’s notice address is 2717 Perseverance Drive, Suite 300, Austin, TX 78731, Attention: Executive Director, with a copy to the same address, Attention: General Counsel; the Consultant’s address is blank. The parties execute the Agreement to be effective as of the date first written above.
